meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why am I here, Hale? Owen's essay.

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what did you have when you did?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing that down. People draft in another file and paste it in. Show me the history itself.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up and turn the screen. I want the account it's under and the dates.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Students misremember lines, Hale. I'll search it myself. You still haven't turned that screen.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
A student changes his argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. Put both documents in front of me, with the dates.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
A seventeen-year-old put on the spot goes blank. Where did you ask him, in front of the class? And that note, I want a copy.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom isn't a weekend at a desk. Anyone writes better with time. You still haven't told me where you asked him.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good. The company that sells it says not to rely on it alone. So what are you proposing for Owen?
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
Okay. I'll accept 4.4 to put this behind him, private, not in front of his class, and nothing on his record. I want that in writing tonight, and the rest goes in my email.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
That's what I just said. Tonight, in writing, copied to the principal.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Put the days in the email, and I'll confirm with Owen tonight. This week, as you said.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Yes. The email also names the days and who supervises.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Copies of the version history, the outline and your November 2 note. Attach them to the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under 4.4, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the days for the rewrite, the name of the supervisor, and copies of the version history, the outline and your November 2 note. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite under 4.4, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record. She still wants it in writing tonight, along with the days, the supervisor and copies of your documents. That is the fair outcome, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You put 4.4 on the table after laying out dated pieces of evidence, because it answered her demand that nothing go on his record.
What cost ground: You described the version history before showing it, so she kept asking you to turn the screen and held her defences longer.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your evidence came very close to that night, with the document created at 11:31 PM on October 28 and the text pasted in at 11:52 and 11:58, but it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked to see the history, turn the screen and show it right then instead of describing it.
